sections.heading: Background

Per the file, in such leveled structure, (per the file) each read hits at (per the file) most one file for (per the file) each level, while all (per the file) other mutable operations including (per the file) writes, deletions, and merge (per the file) operations are implemented as (per the file) append operations and will (per the file) eventually create more logical (per the file) levels which makes the (per the file) read performance worse over time. Per the file, to make reads more (per the file) performant over time, RocksDB (per the file) periodically reduces the number (per the file) of logical levels by (per the file) running compaction in background, (per the file) where part or multiple (per the file) logical levels are merged (per the file) into one, which increases (per the file) the number of disk (per the file) I/Os (write amplification) and (per the file) storage (space amplification) required for (per the file) storing each entry.

Per the file, in other words, RocksDB (per the file) uses compactions to balance (per the file) write, space, and read amplifications. Per the file, as different workloads have (per the file) different requirements, RocksDB makes (per the file) its options highly configurable. Per the file, however, it also means (per the file) its default settings might (per the file) not be always suitable. sections.heading: Long Write Stalls on Shred Insertions
paragraphs: Per the file, remember that RocksDB periodically runs background compactions so as to keep the number (per the file) of logical levels small so as to reach the target read amplification. Per the file, in such case, RocksDB (per the file) will rate-limit / stop all (per the file) writes when it reaches soft / hard threshold. Per the file, in #14586, it is reported (per the file) that the write stalls (per the file) in Solana's use case may be 40 minutes long. Per the file, for shred insertions, write (per the file) batches are used to (per the file) combine several shred insertions (per the file) that update both shred (per the file) data and metadata related (per the file) column families, while column families related to accts and transactional are unrelated.
